rejected/obsolete-quantifier-functions.m.text:
Never-adopted quantifier names

Rejected

## 1. Name and Classification **Never-adopted quantifier names — Rejected.** [Bosak PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77) / [immutable revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525). This is a disposition dossier, not implementation of the refused/deferred shape. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:all-equal](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-all-equal), [fn:some](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-some), [fn:every](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-every). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Prevent guessed function names from becoming accidental compatibility promises. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes REQ-118 records fn:all and fn:some-of as names that never existed in the adopted surface. Use all-equal/all-different for sequence equality and some/every for boolean predicates. These are different contracts; there is no universal mechanical rename from fn:all. ## 5. Motivation Prevent guessed function names from becoming accidental compatibility promises. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Names borrowed from other languages are not XPath aliases. Equality of all values differs from every value satisfying a predicate. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:all((1,1)) ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences REQ-118 records fn:all and fn:some-of as names that never existed in the adopted surface. Use all-equal/all-different for sequence equality and some/every for boolean predicates. These are different contracts; there is no universal mechanical rename from fn:all. Names borrowed from other languages are not XPath aliases. Equality of all values differs from every value satisfying a predicate. ## 12. Implementation The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [all.xpath](../examples/obsolete-quantifier-functions/all.xpath): raises `XPST0017` at mode 40. [some-of.xpath](../examples/obsolete-quantifier-functions/some-of.xpath): raises `XPST0017` at mode 40. [alternative.xpath](../examples/obsolete-quantifier-functions/alternative.xpath): returns `true` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `obsolete-quantifier-functions-all`, `obsolete-quantifier-functions-some-of`, `obsolete-quantifier-functions-alternative`. No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

type-system/choice-types.md.text:
Choice item types

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Choice item types** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-118 S6a; choice item type evidence in VersionGateTests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: choice item types](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-choice-item-types). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #89](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/89), [immutable mainline revision `83d152ff`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/83d152ffdba55fe160f33366fa14ed2922fa2f9d) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Express the permitted alternatives in one item type. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, combine individual instance-of tests with or. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/choice-types/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/choice-types/main.xpath). Both yield `true` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A legacy order identifier can be an integer or a string, but not a fractional amount. Express the permitted alternatives in one item type. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Alternative order affects coercion; the instance-of examples here only test membership and do not perform conversion. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Alternative order affects coercion; the instance-of examples here only test membership and do not perform conversion. ## 8. Structure ```xquery 'PO-8801' instance of (xs:integer|xs:string) ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Express the permitted alternatives in one item type. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. Alternative order affects coercion; the instance-of examples here only test membership and do not perform conversion. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S6-types. Membership, explicit casts and coercion are separate. Cast alternatives are attempted in order; already-matching choice coercion currently converts a string to an earlier integer alternative, contrary to the current matched-alternative rule. K02 retains typed let/argument/return failures with independent expectations. Namespace/type aliases are host-defined, not standalone global registrations. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Membership is distinct from coercion; Already-matching alternatives and ordered coercion of unmatched untyped values; 3.1 choice grammar refusal. **Boundary:** The tested integer/string alternatives do not certify every schema union, function/record alternative or error-precedence combination. Schema union/list context has separate named evidence. Ownership: T03, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/choice-types/main.xpath) yields `true`. The [edge case](../examples/choice-types/edge.xpath) yields `false`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: alternative type matching/coercion. The number and ordering of alternatives affect the work performed. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `choice-types-main`, `choice-types-edge`, `choice-types-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_ChoiceItemType_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_Choice_InstanceOf_AnyAlternativeMatches`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_Choice_Cast_FirstCoercibleAlternativeWins`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

Nominative records: host-defined identity

21 October 2026

## 1. Name and Classification **Bounded XSLT-defined identity is implemented in public1.23.2; this is not a standalone XPath declaration facility or a complete promotion of the historical deferred proposal.** [Current mapping](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). ## 2. Intent Explain why a host-declared name can matter beyond the field shape of a record. ## 3. Also Known As Named/nominal/nominative record identity in the tested XSLT declaration context. ## 4. History / Supersedes The original PR77 disposition at27bc663b and its earlier blanket deferral prose are retained in the [historical snapshot](../../history/REQ126-NOMINATIVE-RECORDS-SNAPSHOT-20261021.md). Later XSLT source supplies bounded named identity. This does not recover historical adopted specification pins or claim a new standalone XPath feature. ## 5. Motivation Distinct application interfaces may share a field named x while requiring different declared identities. ## 6. Language Alignment Unlike a structural alias, nominal identity is not established by matching fields alone. A C# or TypeScript name does not register a type in Bosak; the compiled XSLT declaration provides the tested context. ## 7. Applicability Use the tested XSLT declaration/constructor path. A bare XPath expression without the host-defined type context cannot assume these names are registered. ## 8. Structure Declare t:point and t:other with identical x fields; compare constructor results using instance-of or `record(t:point)` pattern. See complete fixtures rather than treating the name as a globally available XPath keyword. ## 9. Participants [xsl:record-type](../deferred/xslt-record-type.md) supplies the context and constructor; [RecordPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/RecordPattern.cs) tests the value without coercing it. ## 10. Collaborations Structural record aliases can describe field shapes separately; map patterns can inspect keys/entry sequences. None is a synonym for nominal identity. ## 11. Consequences Equal fields need not satisfy a different named type. Binding/function conversion rules require separate evidence; an identity check does not establish every coercion/recursive/package rule. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Host-defined nominal identity differs from plain map shape; Constructor and typed-map coercion paths; Tested select/body/trailing defaults and static constructor/coercion values in Legacy and Xslt40Draft version-4 stylesheets. **Boundary:** Bounded defaults/static fields are verified in both named hosts; no blanket claim of missing support remains for those forms. Import/package identity, visibility, recursion, global-initializer timing and all static override/cast/update combinations still require separate evidence. Ownership: T04. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [nominal-own](../examples/intake-types/nominal-own.xsl), [nominal-other](../examples/intake-types/nominal-other.xsl), [type-nominal-own](../examples/intake-types/type-nominal-own.xsl) and [type-nominal-other](../examples/intake-types/type-nominal-other.xsl) give positive and negative examples. The older standalone [structural alternative](../examples/nominative-records/alternative.xpath) remains unchanged. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses New nominal and record-pattern rows plus [Xslt40RecordPatternTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40RecordPatternTests.cs). No new XPath GatedSets member or upstream acceptance is inferred from host-specific XSLT examples. ## 16. Related Features [Structural records](structural-records.md), [item aliases](../deferred/xslt-item-type.md), [grammar inventory](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md).

type-system/record-updates.md.text:
Record updates with but with

Frozen XPath4.0 - structural record contract

**Public1.23.7 - 23 October2026:** EQName bracket parsing, inline-record signature gates and numeric separator boundaries are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.7-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog74 entries/2,893 documentation checks; REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial. Braid dependency1.23.4 unchanged. Earlier source/unpublished checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Record updates (`but with`)** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S6b. The result is a new record with the original record's type annotation; merged values must satisfy that annotation through coercion. This entry maps existing structural behavior, not a new nominal declaration facility. Delivery: [PR #90](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/90), immutable `ca6e9c27cf4c62953763f800bdef2610ff64789a`; [RecordTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) pins source behavior. Current review pin, refreshed22 October 2026: [expressions XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), `id-with-expression`, `id-item-coercion-rules`, `casting-to-record`, `id-structural-record-types`. This is a current comparison, not a recovered historical adoption pin. The bounded signature-gate correction is in unpublished source 1.23.6; public 1.23.4 already supplies the documented4.0 record behavior. ## 2. Intent Construct a changed record while keeping its declared field constraints and leaving the original value available. ## 3. Also Known As A ButWithExpr performs a record update by construction. It is not an in-place assignment, a database mutation, or the discarded extensible-map proposal. The operands are record(*) and map(*); the record annotation supplies the result type. ## 4. History / Supersedes A 3.1 adapter can select/validate fields, convert values and create a replacement map with map:merge/use-last. The [complete baseline](../examples/record-contracts/report-3.xsl) does that for the stock task. It has no record annotation and is not a universal replacement for record coercion. [The 4.0 report](../examples/record-contracts/report-4.xsl) casts the imported map, then constructs its amended record. ## 5. Motivation A stock feed supplies quantity and delta. The report must show both the imported quantity and adjusted quantity, preserve row order and reject invalid lexical numbers. Record update makes a changed typed value explicit while retaining the before value. [Complete input/output and repair contract](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) makes the task independently runnable. ## 6. Language Alignment This is XPath's annotation-driven reconstruction, not JavaScript object spread or an unrestricted immutable dictionary update. Undeclared fields and noncoercible values fail. A cast may discard surplus keys and convert a lexical string to an integer; update uses coercion and therefore does not automatically perform that lexical cast. Optional empty values are entries whose values are empty, not absent keys. Structural records are distinct from XSLT-defined nominal identity. ## 7. Applicability Use it after establishing the target record annotation. At import boundaries, deliberately select cast versus coercion: cast filters extras; coercion rejects them. Supply correctly typed update values or convert them explicitly. The stock task casts @delta to integer before updating qty. This example permits negative adjustments and does not enforce a nonnegative-stock rule. ## 8. Structure ```xpath ((map{'a':1} cast as record(a as xs:integer)) but with map{'a':2})?a ``` This is the runnable `record-contract-update-value` probe and returns2. The original-preservation probe produces `1|2` from before/after lookups. ## 9. Participants [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) handles record syntax and but-with expressions. [VmEngine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) applies the existing annotation/coercion path. [RecordTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) and the public [documentation runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) provide named evidence; no new public API is added. ## 10. Collaborations Cast constructs the import record, adding a present-but-empty optional note and dropping import-only trace. Update merges the replacement quantity and recoerces to the left annotation. The output keeps the original quantity and adjusted value in a row map. Map access and record lookup are distinct: map:get can inspect a missing key without the record lookup's undeclared-field error. ## 11. Consequences Unknown fields, a plain-map left operand, a non-map right operand and an empty required field raise XPTY0004 in the supplied probes. Integer-to-double promotion is checked; arbitrary string-to-integer update casting is not implied. Optional fields may be set to empty while retaining key presence. Nested structural conversion and declaration order are bounded tested cases, not proof of every composite/nominal type combination. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S6-update. Updates reconstruct under the existing annotation, retain the original value and reject unknown or noncoercible replacement fields. Field order, empty values and nested promotion retain bounded evidence. Do not generalize structural updates to all nominal/static/package/recursive record combinations. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Annotation-preserving reconstruction retains the original value; Unknown fields, plain-map left operand and invalid replacement values refuse; Optional empty values retain key presence; nested promotion and field order are bounded. **Boundary:** Update uses coercion, not lexical import casting. Structural examples do not establish every nominal static/default-field update, method or package context. Ownership: T04, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Thirty-five XPath probes cover cast/coercion/update distinctions; three explicit 3.1 refusal cases and eight complete3.0/4.0 reports bring the slice to46 documentation checks. type-system/typed-let-coercion.md.text:
Typed let coercion

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Typed let coercion** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-123 destructuring/typed-let cluster; local coercion tests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: let expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-let-expressions), [item coercion](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-item-coercion-rules). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129), [immutable mainline revision `b8e4b9f5`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/b8e4b9f510543c04d88a7c10ee2af28808a0fd5c) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent State the type requirement at the binding; integral in-range values can be relabeled. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, an explicit constructor and separate validation express the boundary. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/typed-let-coercion/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/typed-let-coercion/main.xpath). Both yield `true` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A small sensor code must fit the receiving signed-short value space. State the type requirement at the binding; integral in-range values can be relabeled. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Coercion is not truncation. A fractional number cannot be silently relabeled as an integer. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Coercion is not truncation. A fractional number cannot be silently relabeled as an integer. ## 8. Structure ```xquery let $code as xs:short := 42 return $code instance of xs:short ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: State the type requirement at the binding; integral in-range values can be relabeled. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. Coercion is not truncation. A fractional number cannot be silently relabeled as an integer. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S6-record-conversion, REQ123-destructuring. C03 cast/coercion/lookup boundaries remain: casts filter surplus fields, coercion rejects them, optional keys become present empty entries, and ordinary maps are not annotated records. Full composite/nominal/static/default/package and error-eagerness combinations remain unaccepted; bounded nominal defaults from C03 remain supported. Sequence rest/short inputs, array member groups/surplus/short errors, map missing keys, per-variable/whole-pattern types, duplicates and lexical shadowing are mapped. Undeclared annotated-record fields incorrectly bind empty when destructured. K03 retains the required record-lookup XPTY0004 expectation. Plain-map missing-key emptiness remains a different supported contract. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Typed binding/coercion differs from instance-of and cast; Record and numeric promotion with surplus/invalid value refusal; Inline function parameter/result conversion and modern versus paired static/runtime BC controls. **Boundary:** The probe runner explicitly sets both compile-time and runtime BC flags. These controls do not certify all XSLT 1.0/3.0 host propagation, schema-aware constructors or arbitrary function subtyping. C02 atomic-type-annotation empty-input defect remains open. Ownership: T03, T05, F08-atomic-annotation-empty. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. The [record-contract slice](../RECORD-CONTRACTS.md) adds typed-let record promotion and surplus-field refusal probes. A typed binding uses coercion, not an import cast; extra fields are rejected. See [casts versus coercion](structural-records.md) and [record updates](record-updates.md) for the bounded record-specific matrix. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/typed-let-coercion/main.xpath) yields `true`. The [edge case](../examples/typed-let-coercion/edge.xpath) yields `XPTY0004 (expected error)`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: small per-binding type/coercion overhead; complex declared types add their own checks. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `typed-let-coercion-main`, `typed-let-coercion-edge`, `typed-let-coercion-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Evaluate_TypedLet_FrozenXPath40_Coerces`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

Compound template patterns and dispatch

21 October 2026

**C07 lifecycle review — 26 October 2026:** [Current disposition and correction receipts](../LIFECYCLE-RECONCILIATION.md) distinguish delivered scope, retained history and pending acceptance. Six closure workpackages remain; no feature or profile promotion. **Public1.23.4 — 22 October 2026:** Union-minimum and EQName URI-punctuation priority corrections are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.4-PUBLICATION.md). Opening-bracket URI parsing remains separately limited. Earlier unpublished delivery records below are historical. **22 October 2026 — EQName priority correction, source 1.23.4:** Effective 4.0 name-test priority ignores URI punctuation; earlier profiles retain their existing behavior. [Scope, regressions and validation](../EQNAME-PATTERN-PRIORITY.md). Opening-bracket URI parsing remains a separate limitation. Public release remains 1.23.2; REQ-126 stays In Progress. Prior delivery records below retain their historical versions and outcomes. **22 October 2026 — source 1.23.3:** 4.0 node unions now use the minimum alternative default priority, aligned with the pinned current draft. The two catalog reproducers now expect `competitor`; their prior 1.23.2 observations remain recorded. 3.0 dispatch, explicit priorities and single-rule 4.0 `next-match` are preserved. [Correction and validation](../UNION-MINIMUM-PRIORITY.md). Public release remains 1.23.2; REQ-126 stays In Progress. Earlier delivery snapshots below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT 4.0 compound contexts in public 1.26.3.** The union-minimum, EQName URI-priority and opening-bracket parsing corrections are delivered. [C05 review](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) retains their verified scope and the remaining pattern/model limits. [The original review](../COMPOUND-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md) and dated 1.23.x observations remain historical. ## 2. Intent Combine node membership tests and dispatch priorities without confusing set parsing, rule identity or item-pattern context. ## 3. Also Known As Union pattern, intersect/except pattern, grouped XNode pattern and effective-version-sensitive dispatch in the reviewed contexts. ## 4. History / Supersedes The complete3.0 baseline uses predicate conditions and explicit priorities; the4.0 report uses grouped set/union patterns. Earlier technical outputs are observations, not universal semantic equivalence. Original source delivery revisions and historical adoption gaps remain in the review/audit. ## 5. Motivation A manual publisher must hold blocked/draft articles even when other readiness conditions match, while keeping review cases visible and output order stable. ## 6. Language Alignment Pattern operators do not inherit every XPath-expression or C#/SQL precedence intuition. Parenthesized XNode contexts can differ from unparenthesized item patterns. A priority selects a rule after membership; it does not change which nodes satisfy a set expression. ## 7. Applicability Use supporting XSLT contexts with explicit business priorities. Source1.23.3 corrects implicit union priority to the pinned minimum; public1.23.2 retains the recorded discrepancy. ## 8. Structure Reviewed shapes include `(A intersect B) except C`, `A | B`, `A union B` and parenthesized XNode forms. These are descriptive shapes; complete XML namespaces and expression context are in the [reports](../examples/manual-patterns/README.md), not an exhaustive grammar. ## 9. Participants [PatternCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/PatternCompiler.cs) handles validation/membership; [TemplateRule](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/TemplateRule.cs) computes priority and retains rule identity. No public API change. ## 10. Collaborations Combine rule membership with explicit priority, modes, sorted apply-templates and bounded next-match chains. Type/map/array pattern categories are mapped [separately](structured-value-patterns.md). ## 11. Consequences Grouping can change membership;4.0 node unions have a single rule identity in the tested chains. Source1.23.3 uses the pinned minimum alternative priority; public1.23.2 retains maximum. An explicit priority is an application policy, not a conformance fix for the engine. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-compound. Left-associative intersect/except and grouped membership pass. Delivered 4.0 union-minimum priority, EQName URI-punctuation priority and bracket parsing pass; older uncorrected notices remain historical. Earlier-profile priority compatibility, next-match identity and uncommon mixed pattern contexts retain named unit evidence rather than a blanket whole-pattern acceptance. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest cases use default Legacy host with root/local effective3.0/4.0 versions. Local template overrides are tested. No new complete host/module/package/authoring context matrix or gate promotion is claimed. ## 13. Sample Code Run normal, empty and reordered [manual reports](../examples/manual-patterns/README.md). Compare [set-left40](../examples/manual-patterns/set-left40.xsl) and [set-grouped40](../examples/manual-patterns/set-grouped40.xsl). The [union reproducer](../examples/manual-patterns/union-max40.xsl) verifies the source1.23.3 minimum-priority correction; [explicit priority](../examples/manual-patterns/union-explicit40.xsl) is the safe supported control. ## 14. Performance Notes Matching costs depend on operands, candidate count, paths and predicates. Priority/rule storage can affect dispatch work. No measured speedup, benchmark or universal memory result is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses New manual-patterns cases; existing Xslt40SetPatternAssociativityTests, Xslt40UnionPatternTests, Xslt40SetPatternPriorityTests and Xslt40ParenthesizedItemPatternTests are linked in the [review](../COMPOUND-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). The bounded union regressions verify the pinned minimum rule in source1.23.3; the URI-punctuation name-priority limitation is corrected in source1.23.4, while opening-bracket URI parsing remains separately limited. No new qt4tests GatedSets member; AC-03 remains partial. ## 16. Related Features [Structured-value patterns](structured-value-patterns.md), [type inventory](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md), [union-priority finding](../UNION-PRIORITY-ENGINE-FINDING.md), [catalog](../README.md).

xslt-instructions/module-profiles.md.text:
Module and used-package profile propagation

Bosak host policy - bounded executable reference

**C06 host/profile review — 26 October 2026:** [Bounded reconciliation](../HOST-PROFILE-RECONCILIATION.md) maps this entry to current pinned instruction/host rules and named tests. Seven workpackages remain; instruction comparison, complete static-mode evidence and host/adoption limits remain explicit. No acceptance or profile promotion. Earlier notices remain historical. **Public 1.23.8 - 23 October 2026:** The function default-mode fix and host/module profile coverage are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.8-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog:76 entries/3,073 documentation checks. REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial; Braid smoke/acceptance is separate. Earlier source/unpublished/PR checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Module/profile propagation** - implemented Bosak host composition, with an opt-in experimental XSLT draft profile and frozen embedded XPath 4.0. The same compilation host applies to a directly included, imported or used-package module, while expression selection and forwards-compatible validation retain the dependency's own effective version. This is not a new grammar feature or an experimental XPath promotion. Profile implementation: [cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734). This slice depends on the separate [function default-mode fix](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md), [PR416](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/416), source 1.23.8 unpublished; public 1.23.7 is unchanged. Current comparison: [immutable XSLT XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), include/import/use-package/backwards/forwards/modes sections, refreshed on 23 October 2026. This is not recovered historical adoption. [Audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.md). ## 2. Intent Move a transformation function into a dependency without losing the selected compiler host or silently replacing the dependency's declared version with the principal stylesheet's version. ## 3. Also Known As Include/import module loading and used-package compilation. An XSLT package name/package-version here identifies an XML library package; it is distinct from the Bosak NuGet release version. Include, import and use-package are different composition mechanisms, not interchangeable aliases. ## 4. History / Supersedes Each relation has a baseline library at version 3.0 using explicit if/then/else and a version 4.0 library using otherwise. The principal report remains version 3.0 and calls the same quantity function. The six complete report/library pairs in [the task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) run under both hosts. This is Bosak compatibility policy, not a promise that an arbitrary XSLT 3.0 processor can run a 4.0 library. ## 5. Motivation A shared order-quantity function defaults a missing quantity to1 while retaining explicit zero. It can be maintained in one dependency rather than duplicated in a principal template. The examples separate library migration from the principal version and verify namespace, URI and registration setup together with the actual report. ## 6. Language Alignment The current XSLT draft gives included/imported modules and packages their own declaration/static-context rules. Bosak propagates the selected processor host through compilation; it does not overwrite the child version. Legacy's hybrid policy selects embedded XPath by effective version, whereas Xslt40Draft supplies frozen 4.0 even in a 3.0 library. The tests use nonconflicting function names to isolate that policy. They do not establish import precedence, override/accept/expose semantics, or general equivalence between composition mechanisms. ## 7. Applicability Use this reference for one direct include/import edge or one registered used package loaded from local files, compiled with either public host profile. Multi-hop graphs, package version ranges, overrides, schema/static parameters, dynamic evaluate, authoring, streaming, remote/resource-policy behavior and complete default-mode propagation are outside this slice. ## 8. Structure | Dependency effective version | Legacy host | Draft host | |---|---|---| |3.0 | The supplied otherwise expression refuses XPST0003, regardless of principal 3.0/4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds | |4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds, even with a 3.0 principal | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds | | Module3.0 with local function4.0 | Local override enables the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 | | Module4.0 with local function3.0 | Local override refuses the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 | The selected host's forwards-compatible ceiling still applies to the child's effective version:3.0 for Legacy and4.0 for Draft. A future-version principal does not make a known-version child forwards compatible in Draft. scan remains unavailable under both hosts in the supplied 4.0 libraries. ## 9. Participants [XsltCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltCompiler.cs) captures ProcessorProfile and the URI resolver. [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) resolves includes, imports and used packages. [XsltFunctionLibrary.RegisterPackage](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltFunctionLibrary.cs) maps a package name/version to an absolute module URI. The [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) supplies optional per-case package registrations and always cleans them in finally; its existing package-registry collection serializes these tests with other registry users. ## 10. Collaborations An app/main.xsl principal resolves ../library/module.xsl relative to its own file URI for include/import. A package principal uses a synthetic URN and exact package-version 1.0, registered to the corresponding absolute XML file URI before compilation. The library declares p:quantity and its own version. The principal passes each line node, preserves order and sums the returned quantities. Registry setup is caller/test setup; the XML file does not embed a compiler profile. ## 11. Consequences Changing the principal's version alone does not promote a 3.0 dependency in Legacy. A4.0 dependency does not promote unrelated principal expressions either; this entry tests calls into the library, not every caller expression. Unknown attributes on the supplied apply-templates instruction follow the child/local version and inherited host. Those validation probes exposed an independent function default-mode bug: legal success cases raised XTSE0020 after validation. The separate fix preserves their expected results rather than recording the bug as supported behavior. ## 12. Implementation The 114 cases are 66 focused host/version/static/validation/refusal controls and 48 complete report runs. Before package setup the baseline was70pass/44fail:38 missing-registration failures and six default-mode failures. Scoped registrations changed this to105pass/9fail, revealing the same runtime issue in packages too. On the isolated fix all 114 pass with unchanged expected results. The runner adds optional packages metadata and cleanup on both success and failure; rows without it preserve their prior setup. [Machine audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json). ## 13. Sample Code For each relation, [the complete task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) links the baseline and mixed-version principal/library files. With [normal.xml](../examples/module-profiles/normal.xml), both variants under both hosts emit `A=2|B=1|C=0|lines=3;total=3`. Empty input emits `lines=0;total=0`; reordered input changes line order; invalid integer text raises FORG0001. All namespaces, fixtures, dependency locations, package registrations and expected results are supplied. The library expression `(xs:integer($line/@qty) ?? 1)` is actually executed in the4.0 variants. ## 14. Performance Notes These examples verify compilation policy and module loading, not a performance optimization. Each run compiles real local files and may allocate a separate package/module context. No compile-cache, concurrency or timing benefit is claimed. Reusing a compiled executable or resolving larger graphs needs separate measurements and contracts. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `module-profile-include-root4-module3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-root3-module4-legacy`, `module-profile-package-root4-module3-draft40`, `module-profile-package-root4-module4-local3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-validation-root5-module4-draft40`, `module-profile-package-static-root4-module3-draft40` and `module-profile-package-report-module40-normal-legacy`, plus all 114 cases listed in [the audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Named [ProcessorProfileTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ProcessorProfileTests.cs) methods ModulesInheritProfile, ModuleValidationInheritsProfile and UsedPackageInheritsProfile provide independent API evidence. This XSLT host/module contract has no applicable XPath-only gate assignment; no gate is invented or promoted. ## 16. Related Features [Ordinary stylesheet profiles](processor-profiles.md), [otherwise](../operators-and-syntax/otherwise-operator.md), [function default-mode correction](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md) and [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). General package visibility/version resolution, transitive graphs and full lexical default-mode contexts remain follow-ups. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC03 remain partial.

Type, map and array template patterns

21 October 2026

**Compound-pattern follow-up supplied — 21 October 2026:** [New bounded mapping](../COMPOUND-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md) now covers set/union grouping, priority and rule identity, with a separately labelled current-draft union-priority gap. Original counts/queues below describe their earlier checkpoint. ## 1. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT4.0 surface in public1.23.2.** This entry maps tested type, record, map-entry and array-member patterns; it is not the complete pattern grammar. [Pinned source/deliveries](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). ## 2. Intent Dispatch structured values to template rules while keeping key presence, member cardinality, type annotation and nominal identity explicit. ## 3. Also Known As Type pattern, string-key map pattern, array member pattern and named record pattern in their respective reviewed forms. ## 4. History / Supersedes The intake [3.0 baseline](../examples/intake-types/report-3.xsl) uses a named template and explicit predicates. The [4.0 report](../examples/intake-types/report-4.xsl) uses structured-value template patterns. Same results for these fixtures do not establish universal equivalence or a general grammar migration. ## 5. Motivation Route valid line maps and nonempty SKU arrays while making zero quantities and empty bundles visible as review cases. ## 6. Language Alignment Pattern syntax is not XPath constructor syntax. `array(atomic(xs:integer)+)` in match differs from a sequence type in @as. Matching does not perform the annotation/conversion that an @as binding may apply. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer supports the relevant XSLT host/effective-version contract. Prefer the portable named-template form when targeting3.0 processors. ## 8. Structure Reviewed shapes: `~t:shape`, `record(t:point)`, `{'v':.?}`, `{'v':.,*}` and `array(atomic(xs:integer)+)`. Namespace prefixes, context and complete files are in the [example family](../examples/intake-types/README.md). These shapes do not replace the normative grammar. ## 9. Participants [PatternCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/PatternCompiler.cs), [StringKeyMapPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/StringKeyMapPattern.cs), [ArrayPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/ArrayPattern.cs) and [RecordPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/RecordPattern.cs). ## 10. Collaborations Use named aliases for type tests, explicit conversion at bindings, and explicit template priorities where application policy needs them. The report uses disjoint map/array patterns and explicit priorities rather than claiming all default-priority interactions. ## 11. Consequences A closed map pattern rejects extra keys unless opened; optional entry values still require the key. Member occurrence indicators constrain each sequence, not array size. Empty arrays can satisfy universal member constraints; business nonempty checks remain explicit. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [map-empty-present](../examples/intake-types/map-empty-present.xsl) versus [map-empty-missing](../examples/intake-types/map-empty-missing.xsl); [array-vacuous](../examples/intake-types/array-vacuous.xsl) versus [array-empty-member](../examples/intake-types/array-empty-member.xsl); six full [reports](../examples/intake-types/README.md). ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses New intake-types map/array/type rows; [map-entry tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40MapEntryPatternTests.cs), [array tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArrayPatternTests.cs) and [type tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40TypePatternTests.cs). No new qt4tests gate membership; applicable-gate acceptance remains partial. ## 16. xslt-instructions/xsl-select.md.text:
xsl:select: XPath in stylesheet text

21 October 2026

## 1. Name and Classification **xsl:select — implemented Bosak XSLT4.0 surface.** [Body-expression delivery `69a7cfd3`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/69a7cfd3c84e405c037be41786464950d1c06696); [current source review](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md). This entry documents shipped behavior under REQ-126, not a new engine feature. Historical adopted specification revision is not recovered; current review pin is3230573afe246f1b502ed2e22d187ce9928155b1 section `select-instruction`. ## 2. Intent Return an XPath expression result while keeping a multiline expression in XML text or CDATA rather than a quoted XML attribute. ## 3. Also Known As Text-body XPath evaluation. `xsl:sequence/@select` is the earlier alternative, not an alias for the new instruction. ## 4. History / Supersedes The [3.0 dispatch report](../examples/dispatch-grammar/report-3.xsl) uses value-of/attribute expressions; the [4.0 report](../examples/dispatch-grammar/report-4.xsl) uses xsl:select for report fragments. Both explicitly create text. Arbitrary returned maps, arrays and nodes require their own receiving context; text conversion is not universal equivalence. ## 5. Motivation Keep both quote characters, braces and formatting readable in dispatch/report expressions. XML escaping is still needed for ordinary text containing markup delimiters; CDATA avoids those escapes subject to XML's CDATA terminator rule. ## 6. Language Alignment The body is XPath, not JavaScript or an XSLT sequence constructor. Literal braces belong to XPath maps/strings, not AVT or expand-text interpolation. Returning items does not imply writing text nodes. ## 7. Applicability Use when the receiving Bosak host permits the implemented draft surface. Use portable3.0 instructions when portability is required. Validate structured results through their consumer rather than stringifying them unintentionally. ## 8. Structure ```xml ``` Complete namespace/context declarations are in [select-cdata.xsl](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-cdata.xsl). Optional as applies result conversion/type checks. Only permitted leading fallbacks precede expression text; this is a descriptive shape, not a complete grammar. ## 9. Participants [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) validates content and selects expression compatibility; [TransformEngine](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) evaluates it with the caller's context. No new public API is introduced. ## 10. Collaborations Combine with variables/functions for structured values and value-of for explicit text output. The dispatch report uses arrays and switch without flattening away empty batch members. ## 11. Consequences Improves expression readability but adds a draft instruction dependency. Adjacent atomic values can gain separators during tree construction; explicit text construction matters. Optional result types can raise XPTY0004. ## 12. Implementation Default Legacy host uses effective version:3.0 expressions use XPath31,4.0 uses frozen XPath40, and local overrides matter. Known instruction recognition is separate: Bosak accepts the tested simple xsl:select forms under3.0, but this is not portable3.0 syntax. Explicit Xslt40Draft host selects frozen XPath40 independently of local lower version. [Version matrix](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md#recognition-is-distinct-from-compatibility). ## 13. Sample Code Run the complete [report](../examples/dispatch-grammar/README.md) against normal, empty and reordered input. The [focus](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-focus.xsl) and [text-focus](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-focus-text.xsl) files distinguish item results from explicit text. The [required-empty](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-required-empty.xsl) file intentionally fails XPTY0004. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost is dominated by the XPath expression and its result materialization. CDATA changes XML authoring, not an execution complexity guarantee. No measured speed or memory improvement is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses New manifest IDs include dispatch-grammar-select-cdata, select-coercion, select-type-error, select-required-empty, select-focus/text and expression-root30/root40/local30/local40. [Xslt40SelectTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SelectTests.cs) and [ArraySelectNativeBoundaryTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ArraySelectNativeBoundaryTests.cs) supply additional source/native evidence. No applicable XPath qt4tests expression set or new GatedSets member exists for this XSLT instruction; AC-03 acceptance remains partial. ## 16. Related Features [xsl:switch](xsl-switch.md), [xsl:array](xsl-array.md), [catalog index](../README.md), [grammar/type review](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md). Current draft reference: [select-instruction](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#select-instruction); immutable review source is linked in the review.
